entries.meaning: A standard by which something is judged.
examples: Cost was the only criterion that mattered.
The application meets all five criteria.
What criteria are you using to decide?
Each criterion is weighted differently.
These criteria have not changed since 1998.

senses.head: A standard of judgment
examples: Cost was the only criterion that mattered.
The application meets all five criteria.
What criteria are you using to decide?
Each criterion is weighted differently.
These criteria have not changed since 1998.

entries.agreement: plural verb — the criteria are strict
entries.variants: ✗ criterias is doubly wrong — a plural made from a plural
entries.contrast: ✗ This criteria is wrong; say this criterion for one, these criteria for several. The plural takes a plural verb: the criteria are listed below, not ✗ is listed.

entries.meaning: An observable fact or event, especially a remarkable one.
examples: The northern lights are a well-studied phenomenon.
Several phenomena remain unexplained.
Migration is a phenomenon found across species.
Remote work became a global phenomenon.
These cultural phenomena deserve serious study.
At nineteen she was already a phenomenon.

senses.head: Something observed
examples: The northern lights are a well-studied phenomenon.
Several phenomena remain unexplained.
Migration is a phenomenon found across species.

senses.head: A trend or occurrence in society
examples: Remote work became a global phenomenon.
These cultural phenomena deserve serious study.

senses.head: A remarkably talented person
examples: At nineteen she was already a phenomenon.

entries.agreement: plural verb — these phenomena are unexplained
entries.variants: phenomenons is used only of remarkable people — he is one of the great phenomenons of the sport
entries.contrast: ✗ A phenomena is wrong. One is a phenomenon; several are phenomena. The exception is the 'extraordinary person' sense, which takes the English plural phenomenons.

entries.meaning: A self-operating machine; figuratively, a person acting mechanically.
examples: The museum displays an eighteenth-century automaton that writes.
Clockwork automata were the wonder of their age.
Finite automata are a foundation of computer science.
After twelve hours he was working like an automaton.
The staff had been reduced to automatons.

senses.head: A person acting without thought

entries.agreement: plural verb — the automata were built in the 1700s
entries.variants: automata in computer science and horology; automatons in general use

entries.meaning: A cluster of nerve cell bodies; also a harmless cyst near a joint.
examples: The basal ganglia control movement.
Each ganglion relays signals to the spinal cord.
Sensory ganglia lie just outside the cord.
She had a ganglion removed from her wrist.
Both ganglions disappeared on their own.

senses.head: A cyst on a tendon

entries.agreement: plural verb — the ganglia are clustered near the spine
